shape: two people in an ordinary moment; one finally says the thing they never said

slides.text: i was holding the flashlight for him in the cold garage, trying to keep the beam perfectly still.
we never talked much during these projects. just the click of a socket wrench and the smell of lawnmower gas.
he was trying to fix a small engine that had been dead since july, his knuckles gray with dust.
usually, this is where he would tell me to check my oil, or ask if i had enough money for groceries.
but he stopped, wiped his grease-stained hands on a yellow rag, and looked at the wall.
without turning around, he said, [[i'm really glad you came home.]]
we stood there in the cold for another hour, and for once, i didn't mind holding the light.

caption:
some people don't have the words
until they are standing in a drafty garage
with grease on their hands.
send this to him.

#dad #growingup #family #home
alt: a seven-slide story about holding a flashlight for a father in a cold garage, ending with him saying he is glad you came home.
